newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO to hold steady on buying interest.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO to hold steady on buying interest.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices on Monday were expected to hold steady in spite of weaker crude and swaps, traders said.

"The numbers on the physical should drop a little ... paper is drifting down," said a trader with a major oil company. "But with Singapore traders continuing to buy, the physical is a bit on the high side.
Swaps fell to $119.00-$120.00 per tonne from $120.25-$121.00 on Friday.
Traders said there was little market talk with no enquiries heard from China.
But some traders said there was a bit of uncovered requirements into China but buyers were holding back because of high levels.
Supplies were still healthy with one Venezuelan cargo arriving in January while two South Korean refiners still had two to three 30,000 tonne cargoes of fuel oil lifting in January.
